title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: MAX'S BROKEN WRIST
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Max Dufresne, who runs a one-truck tree service in Manchester, New Hampshire.
For thirty years, Max never asked anybody for anything.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE ICE
segments.quote: No man is an island, entire of itself.
segments.author: John Donne
lines: One December morning, her neighbor Leo offered to salt her steps.
Max said, I got it. Then she slipped and broke her wrist. Six weeks, no chainsaw.
At the hospital, her sister texted a line from John Donne, the English writer:
No man is an island, entire of itself.
Max typed back, I'm a woman. Then she let Leo drive her home.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE PICKLE JAR
segments.quote: The first test of a truly great man is his humility.
segments.author: John Ruskin
lines: At home, she fought a pickle jar one-handed. Butter knife. Hammer. Teeth.
Her late mom's fridge magnet quoted the English writer John Ruskin:
The first test of a truly great man is his humility.
Or woman, Max muttered, and carried the jar to Mrs. Pham across the street.
Mrs. Pham is four foot ten. One twist. Pop. She sent Max home with soup.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE CREW
segments.quote: No man will make a great business who wants to do it all himself, or to get all the credit of doing it.
segments.author: Andrew Carnegie
lines: Max had three big jobs before Christmas. Her helper Ty, twenty-four, had never climbed lead.
She almost canceled. Then she saw a clipping from the steel man Andrew Carnegie:
No man will make a great business who wants to do it all himself, or to get all the credit of doing it.
So she stayed on the ground with a radio, and Ty climbed.
The big oak came down exactly where she said.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE HEDGE
segments.quote: Common sense is not so common.
segments.author: Voltaire
lines: Then Max tried to drive her stick-shift truck with one hand.
She parked it, very gently, in Leo's hedge.
Leo leaned in the window and quoted Voltaire:
Common sense is not so common.
She handed Leo the keys. For six weeks, he drove, and talked about mail routes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE STORM
segments.quote: In critical moments even the very powerful have need of the weakest.
segments.author: Aesop
lines: In January, an ice storm dropped a huge maple across Mrs. Pham's driveway.
Ty climbed, Leo hauled, Mrs. Pham poured coffee.
Then Mrs. Pham pointed up. A cracked limb hung over the power line.
Max remembered Aesop, the old Greek storyteller:
In critical moments even the very powerful have need of the weakest.
They cut it down safe.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE WOODPILE
segments.quote: There is no grace in a benefit that sticks to the fingers.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: In February, the cast came off. That maple was now a mountain of firewood.
The old Max would have sold it. But Leo quoted Seneca, the Roman thinker:
There is no grace in a benefit that sticks to the fingers.
So Max and Ty stacked free firewood on every porch on the street.
Then she said three hard words. Thank you, everybody.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Take the help. Stay humble. Share the work. Use sense. Value the small. Give freely.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Take the help. Stay humble. Share the work. Use common sense. Value the small. Give freely.
I asked my neighbor for help once. Now he comes every Sunday and eats my pickles.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
